intro: Two measurements may use different units yet share a linear relationship. Centering and normalizing isolates their direction of association.
task: Compute the Pearson correlation coefficient of paired observations with a defined error for constant inputs.
requirements: x and y are equal-length vectors with at least two observations.
Reject either centered norm at or below 1e-12. Return a scalar clipped to [-1,1] only to correct roundoff.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Positive line
examples.output:
1
(Arrays shown as lists; numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places.)

examples.output:

(Arrays shown as lists; numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places.)

examples.name: Zero linear association
examples.output:

(Arrays shown as lists; numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places.)

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Offsets disappear after centering each vector; positive units disappear after normalizing their lengths.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: A constant vector has no direction after centering, so check its norm before dividing.

explanation: Centering removes offsets, and division by the two vector norms removes positive scale factors. A negative scale flips the sign of the coefficient.
Correlation measures linear association. A zero result does not prove independence: symmetric nonlinear patterns can still have zero centered dot product.
